name: Post-Impressionist Painting
visualIdentity: Expressive directional brushwork, rhythmic color relationships and simplified painted forms. Choose a specific painting reference; Van Gogh’s Starry Night is only one example, not a definition of the movement.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to product and editorial introductions, explanatory or illustrated narratives, museum promos and atmospheric intros. Inferred fit: video or interactive HTML that benefits from layered painted scenes or a drawing-to-paint reveal.
limitations: Avoid assuming swirling skies or using a filter to stand in for an artistic movement. Keep light, color and brush direction coherent. Avoid large parallax that exposes layer edges. Omit chapter transitions when they obscure causality, break a continuous shot or loop, or add no meaningful progression.
palette: Resolve colors from task-provided exact colors, approved brand or reference palette, then existing semantic mappings; the suggested example is last-resort only: background #EEE2C2, foreground #344F60, accents #B58B42, #638873 and #B26B57. Use discrete tokens; gradients are disabled. Preserve approved colors, roles and asset colors. The example foreground/background pair has 6.696 contrast; accents are decorative, not body-text backgrounds. Check actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Animate brush reveals, localized repainting or gentle movement of layered scenery. For interactive HTML, scroll may control chapters or story states; backward scrolling and direct seeks must reproduce coherent states. Keep reading holds and keyboard/reduced-motion support where applicable. For video, use composition time, independent of live input. Avoid default swirling skies, excessive parallax, line boil, generic smoothing or unsupported transitions.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or required audio layer. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied choices. Keep speech clear, avoid competing vocals or clipping, and synchronize picture and sound.
assetRequirements: Prepare painted layers, brush masks or numbered frames with consistent dimensions, transparency and clear naming. Use a consistent reference language and inspect assets before composition. Layer manifests can support separated scenery; preserve source artwork and exact copy.
combinations: Use alone when one painting reference drives the piece. Style-101 layered scenery can add gentle depth while preserving brushwork; style-109 underdrawing can briefly precede paint using the same composition and #344F60 lines, fully replaced by paint. These pairings are explicit suggestions; assess scene fit before use.
productionApproach: Canvas 2D is the recommended style renderer for deterministic brush and layer drawing. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, synchronization, validation and export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, and record why. Keep rendering and motion logic in their own layers; seekable state, seeded randomness and cached or deterministic simulations support reliable video output. For interactive HTML, use scroll-driven states only in that delivery. Inspect representative frames, full playback, audio sync and loop seams.
